summary:
The SP category is the story of the season's final stretch: R1 and R2 are both running hot on starting-pitcher-driven picks at 59-60% over the last 14 days (n=102), a nearly 6-point jump over their season baselines. That matters today because every game on the board carries a clear SP angle. ATL's Chris Sale gets a full four-rating consensus over Luzardo, with R4 showing the widest gap on the slate at +1.07 — and R4's runs category is also hot (60%, +5.5pts over baseline), reinforcing that side rather than fighting it. NYY's Cam Schlittler over Tolle is another unanimous SP-driven pick, and it's the strongest lean by a single rating (R4 NYY +1.29), lining up with R4's blistering 14-day strong-play stretch (27-13, 68%, +21.0u). SDP over CHC is the third full consensus, with R1 leading the way at +0.90 — worth watching since trends+sp is the best-performing category combo all year (57.8%, n=614) and both metrics point the same direction here.

The outlier is CHW @ HOU, where every rating agrees but the edge is thin and negative for Chicago (R1 -0.32 down to R4 -0.18) — treat this as the softest consensus of the day, not a green light. Team trends favor fading it further: NYY is a rare model team that loses value when picked (49%, -5.0u strong), so Houston backers should note the AL contrast even though HOU isn't in that table directly — the point is these thin-margin consensus plays haven't been where the model prints money. Compare that to LAD (71%, n=51, strong 82% +27.0u) and TBR (69%, strong 72% +22.0u) as the gold-standard team profiles when the model actually likes them — today's slate doesn't feature either, so treat all four plays as solid-not-elite. R1's 4-game losing streak in the runs category is a caution flag; lean on SP and trends instead, both riding 3W streaks across R1-R3 and showing the best 14-day strong-play returns of the year (R1 70%, R3 70%, R4 68%).
